Proffit · Syndromes — Spot & Differentiate

Built for the exam stem “this child has… → which syndrome?” Each card pairs the real Ch 5 photo with the one feature that tells it apart from its look-alikes, plus the trap buzzword. Start with the clusters, then drill the cards. Tap a chip or search any gene/feature.

★ Spot-the-syndrome — the confusable clusters start here

The groups exam questions hide in. Learn the one differentiator per row, then the trap.

Midface deficiency → Class III look

Crouzonsynostosis + bulging eyes (exorbitism), normal hands
ApertCrouzon features + syndactyly (fused fingers/toes)
Achondroplasiadwarfism; deficit is the cranial base; mandible normal
Downtrisomy 21 + macroglossia + hypotonia
Fetal alcoholsmooth philtrum, thin lip, short eye fissures

⚠ Trap: Crouzon vs Apert = the HANDS (syndactyly = Apert). Both are FGFR2.

Facial asymmetry — which way does the chin point?

Hemifacial microsomiaundergrowth → chin to the SAME (small) side; microtia
Condylar fracture (child)acquired undergrowth → chin to the affected side
Hemimandibular hyperplasiaovergrowth → chin to the OPPOSITE side; ~85% female

⚠ Trap: Deficiency → chin toward the small side. Overgrowth → chin AWAY (to the opposite side).

Symmetric vs one-sided mandibular deficiency

Treacher CollinsSYMMETRIC (bilateral) + coloboma + downslanting eyes; AD, TCOF1
Hemifacial microsomiaUNILATERAL + microtia; 2nd commonest facial birth defect

⚠ Trap: Symmetric & downslanting = Treacher Collins. One-sided = microsomia.

Too FEW vs too MANY teeth

Ectodermal dysplasiamissing teeth (oligodontia), conical teeth, can't sweat, sparse hair
Cleidocranial dysplasiaextra teeth (supernumeraries), delayed eruption, absent clavicles

⚠ Trap: Ectodermal = MISSING + conical. Cleidocranial = EXTRA + delayed + clavicles. Opposite tooth counts.

Progressive / acquired retrognathia

Juvenile idiopathic arthritisbilateral condylar resorption → “bird face” + open bite
Pierre Robinsequence: micrognathia → glossoptosis → U-cleft + airway at birth

⚠ Trap: JRA = bilateral, autoimmune, progressive. Robin = a birth SEQUENCE (airway first).

Genetic & developmental syndromes 8

Crouzon

craniofacial dysostosis
FGFR2 (±FGFR3)

Premature coronal-suture synostosis, midface hypoplasia, exorbitism (shallow orbits make the eyes look like they bulge).

★ Tell it apart: Synostosis + bulging eyes but HANDS ARE NORMAL — that is what separates it from Apert.

Ortho: Maxillary deficiency → Class III, crowding, high airway/OSA risk. 5

⚠ exorbitism + normal hands + FGFR2

vs Apert · Achondroplasia

Apert

acrocephalosyndactyly
FGFR2

Crouzon-like synostosis PLUS syndactyly of the hands & feet (“mitten” hands); severe midface hypoplasia.

★ Tell it apart: It IS Crouzon + syndactyly — the fused fingers/toes are the giveaway.

Ortho: Severe maxillary deficiency, Class III, very crowded high-arched (often cleft) palate. 5

⚠ syndactyly = Apert (not Crouzon)

vs Crouzon

Achondroplasia

commonest short-limb dwarfism · AD
FGFR3 (autosomal dominant)

Deficient endochondral growth of the CRANIAL BASE → midface deficiency; the mandible is normal-sized.

★ Tell it apart: Dwarfism + the deficit is the cranial base; mandible is normal → only a RELATIVE prognathism.

Ortho: Skeletal Class III (relative mandibular prognathism), midface retrusion. 5

⚠ cranial-base defect, FGFR3, dwarfism

vs Crouzon

Down syndrome

trisomy 21
trisomy 21

Midface deficiency, macroglossia, generalized hypotonia, brachycephaly, hypodontia.

★ Tell it apart: Trisomy 21 + large protrusive tongue + floppy tone — the macroglossia drives the open bite.

Ortho: Class III tendency, anterior open bite, hypodontia, delayed eruption, high periodontal risk. 25

⚠ macroglossia + hypotonia + trisomy 21

Ectodermal dysplasia

hypohidrotic, X-linked
ectodermal (EDA) genes

Thin sparse hair, ABSENT sweat glands (heat intolerance), conical teeth, oligodontia/anodontia.

★ Tell it apart: “Can't sweat + sparse hair + conical teeth” — THE answer when many teeth are congenitally MISSING.

Ortho: #1 cause of multiple congenitally missing teeth; reduced lower-face height. 5

⚠ conical teeth + hypohidrosis + oligodontia

vs Cleidocranial dysplasia

Cleidocranial dysplasia

RUNX2 / CBFA1
RUNX2 (CBFA1)

Absent/hypoplastic clavicles (shoulders approximate), frontal bossing, delayed suture closure.

★ Tell it apart: EXTRA teeth + delayed eruption + missing clavicles — the mirror-image of ectodermal dysplasia (which is MISSING teeth).

Ortho: Delayed eruption, multiple supernumeraries, retained primary teeth, pseudo-anodontia. 35

⚠ supernumeraries + clavicles + delayed eruption

vs Ectodermal dysplasia

Treacher Collins

mandibulofacial dysostosis · AD
TCOF1 (±POLR1C/D)

SYMMETRIC deficiency of the zygoma & mandible, downslanting palpebral fissures, lower-lid coloboma, ear anomalies.

★ Tell it apart: SYMMETRIC + downslanting eyes + coloboma — separates it from the one-sided hemifacial microsomia.

Ortho: Severe mandibular deficiency → Class II, anterior open bite, airway compromise. 5

⚠ symmetric + downslant + coloboma + TCOF1

vs Hemifacial microsomia

Hemifacial microsomia

craniofacial microsomia / Goldenhar
1st & 2nd arch developmental

UNILATERAL deficient ramus/condyle, microtia, soft-tissue deficiency, facial asymmetry. Goldenhar adds epibulbar dermoid + vertebral anomalies.

★ Tell it apart: UNILATERAL (asymmetric) + microtia — the 2nd most common facial birth defect after clefts.

Ortho: Occlusal cant, chin deviates TO the deficient side, midline shift. 5

⚠ unilateral + microtia; Goldenhar = + eye dermoid

vs Treacher Collins · Condylar fracture

Clefts & craniosynostosis 3

Cleft lip & palate

≈1/700 · 70% non-syndromic
multifactorial

Failure of fusion of the facial/palatal processes; uni- or bilateral, complete or incomplete. ~30% syndromic.

★ Tell it apart: The lateral incisor at the cleft site is often missing or malformed; maxilla collapses especially AFTER surgical repair (scar tissue).

Ortho: Maxillary deficiency, anterior/posterior crossbites, missing lateral; needs NAM, alveolar graft, team care. 57

⚠ 1/700, 70% non-syndromic, lateral at the cleft

Craniosynostosis

1/2200 · 25% syndromic
FGFR1/2/3 · TWIST1

Premature fusion of one or more cranial sutures distorts skull shape; ideal surgical release at 3–9 months.

★ Tell it apart: Isolated suture fusion; when syndromic the usual culprits are Crouzon / Apert (FGFR).

Ortho: Skull & orbital distortion; midface effects in the syndromic forms. 5

⚠ 1/2200, 25% syndromic, release 3–9 months

vs Crouzon · Apert

Pierre Robin

a SEQUENCE, not a syndrome
± Stickler (60% syndromic)

Micrognathia → glossoptosis → U-shaped cleft palate + airway obstruction at birth (a cascade = a sequence).

★ Tell it apart: A SEQUENCE (one defect cascades): the triad starts with the small jaw; AIRWAY is the priority; the mandible may ‘catch up’.

Ortho: Small mandible may show catch-up growth; early airway management comes first. 5

⚠ sequence + triad + airway + Stickler

vs Treacher Collins

Acquired & asymmetry causes 9

Childhood condylar fracture

acquired
trauma to the condyle

Injury to the condylar growth site → asymmetric mandibular deficiency; ankylosis risk if untreated.

★ Tell it apart: ACQUIRED unilateral undergrowth from trauma — chin to the AFFECTED side (like microsomia but with a trauma history).

Ortho: Unilateral mandibular deficiency, chin deviation to the affected side, possible ankylosis. 5

⚠ trauma history + chin to affected side

vs Hemifacial microsomia

Juvenile idiopathic arthritis

JIA / JRA · TMJ
autoimmune

BILATERAL condylar resorption → progressive mandibular deficiency (“bird face”).

★ Tell it apart: BILATERAL + progressive + autoimmune → retrognathia + anterior open bite + steep mandibular plane.

Ortho: Retrognathia, anterior open bite, steep mandibular plane angle. 5

⚠ bilateral condylar resorption = bird face

Hemimandibular hyperplasia

condylar overgrowth · ~85% female
condylar overgrowth

Gradual UNILATERAL mandibular overgrowth.

★ Tell it apart: OVERgrowth → chin deviates to the OPPOSITE side (mirror of a deficiency); wait until growth stops before treating.

Ortho: Occlusal cant, chin to the opposite side; treat after growth ceases. 5

⚠ overgrowth → chin to OPPOSITE side

vs Condylar fracture · Hemifacial microsomia

Acromegaly

GH excess (adult)
pituitary GH excess

Adult mandibular overgrowth with spacing; enlarged hands, feet, and brow.

★ Tell it apart: ADULT-onset prognathism + new spacing — the only one that appears AFTER growth is finished.

Ortho: Adult skeletal Class III with arch spacing. 5

⚠ adult onset, pituitary GH, spacing

Fetal alcohol syndrome

teratogen: alcohol
ethanol, 1st trimester

Central midface deficiency, short palpebral fissures, SMOOTH philtrum, thin upper lip, developmental delay.

★ Tell it apart: Smooth philtrum + thin upper lip + short eye fissures + maternal-alcohol history.

Ortho: Midface deficiency → Class III tendency. 5

⚠ smooth philtrum + maternal alcohol

Torticollis

SCM contracture
neck-muscle contracture

Tonic sternocleidomastoid contraction twists the head and restricts growth.

★ Tell it apart: A NECK-muscle problem producing positional plagiocephaly/asymmetry (not a primary jaw defect).

Ortho: Facial asymmetry / plagiocephaly. 5

⚠ SCM contracture, wry neck

Masseter / motor-nerve deficiency

muscle agenesis
muscle / nerve loss

Underdevelopment of bone where the muscle attachment/function is missing.

★ Tell it apart: Living proof of the functional-matrix theory — no muscle pull → deficient bone on that side.

Ortho: Asymmetric facial deficiency on the affected side. 5

⚠ functional matrix; muscle agenesis

Decreased muscle activity

e.g. muscular dystrophy
weak musculature

Low occlusal/masticatory force lets the posterior teeth over-erupt.

★ Tell it apart: Weak muscles → long lower face + open bite (low force = unchecked posterior eruption).

Ortho: Long lower face, anterior open bite. 5

⚠ weak muscles → long face + open bite

X-ray

Dilaceration

trauma to a developing tooth
trauma to the tooth bud

Sharp angulation of the crown/root after the developing tooth is displaced by trauma.

★ Tell it apart: Bent root from an earlier injury to the bud → eruption failure; seen on the radiograph.

Ortho: Eruption failure / difficult or impossible alignment. 5

⚠ bent root from trauma to the bud
